thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 triggered: increased 5xx rate for cross-region requests into eu-west2 starting ~4260001100. Alerts show spike in region-routing errors and elevated latency. Auto-fallbacks tripped for several routes.

eric (oncall): I'm up. Paging in — seeing a bunch of errors from client telemetry. Any idea if this is DNS or steering?

maria (sre): Looking at routing telemetry now. Health checks for eu-west2 control plane look green, but we have an unusual surge of 'route-not-found' responses from the geo-router at the steward layer.

devin (netops): Seeing anomalous BGP churn from one AZ (eu-west2-b). Route fanout remains fine, but pinning decisions appear to be oscillating. Could be a policy feedback loop with recent TTL reduction.

eric (oncall): Oncall checklist: 1) Confirm customer impact; 2) Try quick mitigations (increase TTL, disable noisy policy); 3) If needed, pin affected customers to last-known-good region.

olivia (support): We're seeing support tickets from two customers reporting 502/504s and higher latency in EU. Customer A is on dedicated, Customer B on hosted API. They're both getting fallback responses to us-east.

maria (sre): Correlating traces — prefixes from eu-west2 are intermittently returning 404-ish control-plane responses that the routing layer treats as transient, triggering fallback. The fallbacks then change traffic distribution which then triggers more transient responses. Looks like a feedback oscillation.

devin (netops): I can roll back the last policy change that reduced route TTL (deployed ~4260001000). That might stop rapid churn. Recommend increasing TTL to 60s and disabling the aggressive latency steer for eu-west2 for now.

eric (oncall): Do it. maria, if we increase TTL we should also temporarily disable auto-fallbacks for pinned routes to avoid thrash.

maria (sre): Copy. I'm going to run the plan: 1) disable aggressive latency steering for eu-west2; 2) increase route TTL to 60s; 3) suppress automatic fallback for pinned routes for next 10m. I'll post commands.

incidents-bot: action_log: runbook step start: disable-steer eu-west2 --commit 4260001125

devin (netops): Ran rollback for TTL change: set route_ttl=60s (applied to eu-west2) — verifier shows stable route cache on control plane.

maria (sre): Disabled aggressive steer and suppressed fallback for pinned routes (suppression-window=600s). Monitoring propagation across edge.

eric (oncall): Early signs: error rate dropped ~40% and fallbacks reduced. Latency still elevated for a small subset, but trending down.

olivia (support): Notified affected customers: "We're investigating cross-region routing anomalies causing elevated errors; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 10 minutes."

incidents-bot: metrics: 5xx_rate eu-west2 peaked at 3.2% at 4260001112, down to 1.1% at 4260001165 after mitigations.

maria (sre): Next: collect control-plane logs for the window 4260001080-4260001160 (exports queued). Also create a small eval harness to reproduce steer oscillation with synthetic latency signals.

devin (netops): I see a noisy telemetry feed from one probe cluster in eu-west2-b that was overreporting outage. Raised an internal ticket to investigate probe agent (NET-4390). Could be a probe bug triggering steer.

eric (oncall): Good catch. Action items: (1) devin follow NET-4390 for probe agent fix; (2) maria run postmortem template and include runbook gap on fallback suppression config; (3) olivia continue customer comms with ETA 60m.

olivia (support): Sending update now to affected customers.

maria (sre): Will keep the suppression window up until control-plane logs are analyzed; reopening automatic fallback only when we confirm probes are sane.

eric (oncall): If anything regresses ping @eric and escalate to infra-leads. For now, keeping incident P1 and we'll re-evaluate at 4260001180. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident status updated to "monitoring" at 4260001170 by eric (oncall).

incidents-bot: runbook note: probable root cause = noisy probe telemetry in eu-west2-b causing routing steer oscillation + low TTL amplifying thrash. Further analysis required.

maria (sre): Logged follow-up tasks in the postmortem board. I'll grab control-plane logs and a sampling of affected requests for deeper trace analysis.

eric (oncall): Closing coordination in thread; continue async on postmortem and NET-4390. Last update here at 4260001180.
notes: Slack thread: live incident coordination for cross-region routing oscillation caused by noisy telemetry and short route TTL. Contains incident-bot actions, oncall handoff, mitigation steps, customer comms.
